correctness.rationale: DFT orthogonality for N>=6 exactly extracts C0, C1 and C2 at each window position. Equality of C2 forces the ratio g/f to alternate only two unit phases because the step-two parity cycles have odd order. Equality of C1 either identifies these phases or imposes unimodular successive correlation ratios, hence a two-periodic a_t, constant f_{t+2}/f_t, and an mth-root multiplier. The relative parity phase is uniquely solved. Conversely direct autocorrelation substitution proves that this phase produces identical measurements. The proof covers all allowed N and all complex nowhere-zero f; integer and numerical tests are supplemental and were run from the supplied source file.
unproved_limits: The theorem does not treat N divisible by four, vanishing f entries, or unequal tap amplitudes.

originality.rationale: The statement classifies the full projective measurement fiber for every nowhere-zero complex signal at a fixed equal three-point cyclic STFT window in all cyclic dimensions congruent to two modulo four. The original generic recovery results do not determine exceptional fibers, and the 2023 separated-signal theorem does not apply to nowhere-zero signals. Explicit comparison with the closest two-tap and endpoint-lag recovery claims shows neither logically dominates the three-tap even-order classification. Absence of indexed equivalent sources is not proof of novelty; unindexed specialized calculations remain a risk.

value.rationale: The simplest equal three-tap overlapping Fourier measurement has a generic uniqueness theorem but its exact nowhere-zero exceptional fibers matter for deterministic reliability. This result identifies every failure, bounds fiber size sharply by two independent of length, shows a concrete nonunique pair for every N congruent to two modulo four, and explains why the odd parity-cycle arithmetic collapses the amplitude freedom. The result is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary isolated finite case.
